login.note: The landing page IS the login form (handle or email + password, or 'Sign in with a different account' for a self-hosted PDS). No SSO, no QR. An app password from Settings works here too and is the safer thing to type into a shared browser profile. On success the client writes the session into localStorage under BSKY_STORAGE for this origin only.

logout.note: There is no logout URL. Sign out from Settings > Account > Sign out, or from the account switcher. Clearing cookies does NOTHING here — the session lives in localStorage; the equivalent nuke is removing the BSKY_STORAGE key, which also throws away every remembered account and every client preference in the same blob.

traps: Signing out does NOT remove the account from BSKY_STORAGE — social-app leaves the entry in session.accounts[] with did and handle intact and only strips accessJwt/refreshJwt (both are optional in its zod schema, exactly so an expired session can persist). A probe that gates on 'a handle is in localStorage' reports a signed-out profile as live.

The persisted blob is validated as ONE zod schema, and social-app's own schema.ts warns that a single failing field makes tryParse discard the ENTIRE persisted state — every account and every preference — so the app boots logged out with defaults. A version skew can therefore turn a working session into 'never signed in' with no error anywhere.

BSKY_STORAGE is written asynchronously and fanned out across tabs over a BroadcastChannel ('BSKY_BROADCAST_CHANNEL'); the project's own issue reports the write landing 15-20s later in a throttled/background tab. Probing immediately after a hand login or logout can read the PREVIOUS state. Wait, or re-probe.

No cookie on bsky.app means anything. The app is a pure client: reads and writes are XRPC calls to the account's PDS / the AppView carrying a Bearer token from localStorage. Cookie-shaped reasoning (and any credentialed same-origin fetch) is noise here.

bsky.app is one client of many for the same account. A session here is not a session on the PDS host (bsky.social) or on any other atproto client, and logging out here does not revoke anything server-side.
notes: PROBE STRATEGY: (a) the site's own embedded state object. Bluesky is the exception to the cookie rule in the other site files — there is no session cookie at all. The web client persists {session:{accounts[],currentAccount}} to localStorage under the literal key 'BSKY_STORAGE' (confirmed in bluesky-social/social-app, src/state/persisted/index.web.ts: `const BSKY_STORAGE = 'BSKY_STORAGE'`, and the account/currentAccount shape in src/state/persisted/schema.ts). The probe reads that key, requires a currentAccount.did AND a matching accounts[] entry that still holds a token, and reports the handle. A DOM check (composeFAB / profile link) is appended to `why` as corroboration only — it can be legitimately absent on a route that has not rendered, so it must never flip the verdict. The probe returns a handle or a did and NEVER a token. localStorage is origin-scoped, so this probe is only meaningful on the bsky.app origin. WHAT A READ RECIPE SHOULD DO: not scrape the DOM. Take the account's `service`/`pdsUrl` and accessJwt out of BSKY_STORAGE and call XRPC directly: app.bsky.feed.getTimeline (home feed), app.bsky.feed.getAuthorFeed?actor=<did> (one account), app.bsky.notification.listNotifications, each as GET <service>/xrpc/<nsid> with `Authorization: Bearer <accessJwt>`. Public, unauthenticated reads of public data can go to https://public.api.bsky.app/xrpc/... with no token at all, which is the cheaper path when no session is needed. An expired accessJwt returns 400 ExpiredToken and is refreshed with com.atproto.server.refreshSession using the refreshJwt — a read recipe should treat ExpiredToken as 'refresh', not as 'logged out'. WRITE: left empty on purpose. Posting is com.atproto.repo.createRecord on app.bsky.feed.post and is genuinely easy, but no verb exists here yet and an unverified write path in this file would read as a green light nobody has driven.
probe_checked: 2026-09-12: ran live in the fork and returned a clean signed_out verdict (no throw, no 'no verdict'). The signed-OUT path is proven; the signed-IN path is still a hypothesis.
